title: When You Break One

launchpad.outcome: Break a rule (it happens), skip the shame spiral, and turn it into an IF / THEN response.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What will I do when this trigger shows up again?

say: You missed a winner this morning.
Then you chased the next one.

options.label: Punish yourself: no trading for a week

say: But it teaches you nothing about next Tuesday at 10:04, when the same trigger shows up.

options.label: Ignore it. Tomorrow’s a new day.

say: Then the trigger stays exactly where it is, waiting for you.
Which rule? What happened right before? What were you trying to get or avoid?
What will you do next time that trigger shows up?

beats.principle: DON’T JUST JOURNAL WHAT YOU DID WRONG. JOURNAL WHAT YOU’LL DO WHEN THE TRIGGER RETURNS.

slides.title: You chased.
scenario: You missed the previous winner (no retest).

options: No market entry after a missed retest
action.correct: No market entry after a missed retest

slides.thenPrefill: screenshot it, mark it MISSED ACCORDING TO PLAN, and wait for a new valid setup
slides.punch: Saved. The next time a missed winner shows up, your answer is already written.

slides.fallbackLine: A missed winner often creates an urge to chase the next one.
slides.punch: This is what the Academy shows you whenever this trigger comes back.

slides.quote: A broken rule is data about a trigger. Turn it into a plan, not a punishment.

slides.prompt: What will you do the next time your trigger shows up?
slides.modelAnswer: I review it: which rule, what happened right before, what I wanted, and IF this trigger happens again THEN what I’ll do. No shame, just a plan.

remember: JOURNAL WHAT YOU’LL DO WHEN THE TRIGGER RETURNS.
